text.tspan: Germany's smallest Anbaugebiet (462 ha) on warm Odenwald foothills; the 'Spring Garden of
Under 0.5% of Germany's wine output and just 23 Einzellagen — a genuine boutique region
Phylloxera-free until 2005 (last German region hit) — became Germany's vine nursery and PiWi breeding ground
Sole VDP estate Domaene Bergstrasse (wine made by Kloster Eberbach); two co-ops farm ~85% of vineyards
Yes; about one-third of vineyards are
Both dry and Praedikat; Trocken share
Located in Hessen — the same Bundesland as Rheingau
Two Bereiche: Starkenburg (~85%, best sites) and isolated Umstadt
GG grapes: Riesling, Grauburgunder, Spaetburgunder and Weissburgunder
Hessische ≠ Badische Bergstrasse — different Bundesland and Anbaugebiet
Roter Riesling is a distinct grape (pink/white skins, reintroduced 1991)
Almost no wine is exported — local/tourist demand, not a quality issue
Best sites: Heppenheim Centgericht and Bensheim Kalkgasse
Odenwald shelter, early spring warmth, eastward wind, Rhine
